expected_return.window: scorebord: BUY 13:30 ET on the entry day; SELL amc at the next open, bmo at 13:00 ET on the report day; gross

note: Each member is reported as a percentile of its own live range, 0-100 (pct), with its direction in side; panel_pct (0-100) is the size of the mean of the signed percentiles and side its direction; panel_pct_sd their spread. The selection is panel_pct in the top 20%. panel_score is the signed median of the members' sizes, each read against its own recent history. consensus_k counts members that put the name in their own top 20% on the panel's side; that, not sign agreement, is what selected well on the development names. Certainty (p_up) is recorded and decides nothing. expected_edge_pct is a shrunk in-sample prior, not a forecast. Research only.

opus5.note: Item 0 is the classic shape that has paid here: three counterparty primary documents (tn.gov Standard and Value formularies, Aetna 2027 ACCF list) removing VASCEPA for 2027 that sit on benefit sites rather than the wire, with no 8-K and no analyst mention, against a 2024 precedent of -6.2%; sized at roughly half the conditional move because what resolves inside the window is only whether the Q3 call surfaces it, with the 2027 P&L effect correctly outside, and a ~$15/ADS cash floor under a $12 stock.

opus55.note: Rests on item 0: CVS/Aetna formulary documents dropping VASCEPA for 2027 are unpriced counterparty evidence the first call must address, cushioned by trading below net cash.

sonnet55.note: CVS Caremark 2027 formulary removal of Vascepa (item 0, primary counterparty documents, no 8-K or coverage) on a thin two-analyst name whose 2024 analogue fell 6%; cash above price cushions it.

fable51.note: Rests on item 0: three counterparty formulary documents (CVS Caremark Standard Control, Value Formulary, Aetna ACC, all dated 2026-10-01) remove VASCEPA from 2027-01-01 with no 8-K, no wire and no analyst mention, on a name whose outlook-driven prints moved -9.5% and -11.3% and whose 2024 PBM loss took -6.2%; the Q3 call is the first place 2027 payer status must be addressed, and the net-cash cushion ($15/ADS against $12) plus the chance management stays quiet keep p_up at 30 rather than lower.

opus5.note: Items 0 and 1 are one coherent, quantified mechanism - a Q3 bar set 2.8% BELOW Q2 when Q3 has been at or above Q2 in each of the last three years, with FY consensus exactly at the guide midpoint so a fourth raise would clear it - and this name has bought revenue beats three prints running (+6.85, +3.78, +7.76); sized below a primary-document number because the seasonality is an inference from history rather than a disclosed figure, and kept apart because they land on different lines, with the absence of the pre-announcement management used last October (item 2) cutting the large-miss tail.

opus55.note: Items 0-2: the Q3 consensus sits below Q2, against three years of Q3 at or above Q2, on a name that buys beats and raises; management pre-announced its last miss and has filed nothing this time.

sonnet55.note: Q3 consensus sits below Q2 revenue despite three years of flat-or-higher Q3 seasonality (item 0) and a raise-every-print guide pattern; the name has been buying beats, but this is an inference from history.

fable51.note: Item 0 carries it: a two-source $68.5m Q3 bar sits 2.8% below Q2's $70.5m while Q3 has matched or exceeded Q2 in each of the last three years per the company's own releases, on a name that bought its last three revenue beats (+6.85, +3.78, +7.76) and raised the guide at every print (item 1); no pre-announcement where last year's miss was pre-released (item 2) lowers the miss tail, and the only offsets are a guided set-deployment FCF step-back (item 4) and a proxy that nets to zero (item 5).

opus5.note: Item 1 is the only item that lands on the new information in this release - Lam's 21 October call saying supplier demand is rising faster than Lam itself, that it is pushing suppliers to add capacity, and a preliminary 2027 WFE above $200B - into a stock down 37% in 20 days with a balanced skew and short interest falling 12%; it is halved because Lam's own December guide is only +4.6% q/q with China domestic down against a +12% q/q Q4 consensus, and item 0's beat is capped hard by the reaction function (0 up and 5 down, including -5.19% on a 10% beat with a raise) with the second straight negative operating cash flow quarter (item 4) the mechanism the market has already sold twice.

opus55.note: Small positive lean from Lam's +22% q/q (item 0) and a sector-driven drawdown (item 2), held near 50 because the beat lands inside the guide on a name that sold its last five prints and the Q4 guide is two-sided.

sonnet55.note: Lam's +22% q/q September quarter against a UCTT consensus fixed at the guide midpoint (item 0), after a sector-driven 37% drawdown; tempered because all five prior prints fell and negative operating cash flow is likely.

fable51.note: Item 0 is a counterparty primary document landing after the company last spoke: Lam's +22% q/q September quarter against a UCTT guide midpoint of +12.4% with consensus still at that midpoint the day after Lam printed, corroborated by AMAT's +12% systems guide, plus Lam saying suppliers' demand is rising faster than Lam and pushing them to add capacity (item 1, with the +4.6% December guide and China weakness netted inside it); the -37% sector drawdown with falling short interest and balanced skew (item 2) leaves room to re-rate, but five of five prior windows closed down including a beat-and-raise at -5.2%, so p_up stays near 50 and the 12.3% implied move sets the scale.

opus5.note: Nothing here is unpriced information: items 1 and 2 are a +25%/+50% run-up into a no-call, no-guide release on a name that fell on 5 of 7 prints, which is the free control wearing a finding's clothes (its own independence says it rests on the baseline tape), merged and sized small; the 13D buyer at a $0.31-0.39 cost base damps the downside tail, the bar is single-source so the FFO item is capped, and items 4-6 are a priced non-event, a macro proxy the company has not tracked and a two-sided strategic tail with no timing.

opus55.note: Mild negative lean from item 1 (a +50% run-up into a no-call, no-guide release on a name that fell on 5 of 7 prints), partly offset by the 13D buyer's support; the bar is single-source.

sonnet55.note: Balanced: the 13D buyer's support (item 0) against a 25% run-up into a no-call print with a single-source bar and falling occupancy; nothing decisive.

fable51.note: A +50% run off the Oct 5 low into a no-call, no-guide release with no filed transaction (items 1 and 2), on a name that fell on 5 of 7 prints, against a 13D buyer with a $0.31-0.39 cost base (item 0) that damps the downside; the strategic-review tail (item 6) cuts both ways and nets to zero, and the single-source $0.02 FFO bar caps everything small.

opus5.note: The two large items point opposite ways and that is the honest read: a 24.6% short base at 12.7 days to cover is a real squeeze mechanism (item 1) but the -15 vol-point skew and the +13% five-day run-up say upside is already being paid, while item 3 is the asymmetry - a 55% headcount cut, SG&A down to $19.0m and a CCO in post since 18 August going into the first launch call with about four weeks of data against $600M-$1B peak-sales models - netted against the Cantor view in its own independence, with the open S-3ASR capping any pop.

opus55.note: Near-balanced: a crowded short with call skew (item 1) against a thin commercial team's first launch metrics after a +13% run-up (item 3) and an open shelf (item 4).

sonnet55.note: A 24.6% short base with 12.7 days to cover and upside-paid skew into the first launch call (item 1), offset by the open shelf and a reduced commercial team; the baseline already shows much of the lean.

fable51.note: Near-balanced: a 24.6% short base at 12.7 days to cover with calls bid over puts (item 1) gives any credible week-4 launch metric a squeeze mechanism, but the -15 skew and the +13% five-day run-up say that is largely in the price, the 55% workforce cut and a CCO in post since Aug 18 (item 3) make slow-looking first metrics a real risk, the open shelf (item 4) caps a pop, and the single-source bar caps all sizes; abs set above the indicative 8.9% implied for the crowded short on a first launch call.
